_doc: 教程声明（T1–T4）：每一步的 items 只能点名已声明的指标 / 定义类 / 对象；正文不打字面数字（数字由编译出的 SQL 现算）；必须有一步专门教“按名拒绝”。
title: 从一个数字走回它的口径
intro: 这份数据是一批简历和一批职务说明书算出来的招聘季快照。教程的每一步都指向一条已声明的口径；当你点“运行”，数字由编译出的 SQL 现算，而不是写在正文里。

steps.title: 一个岗位有多少人过线
steps.body: 过线人数数的是被蕴含为这个岗位定义类成员的候选人行。它不读合成分、不读名次——合成分只决定先看谁。所以这个数是下界：没读到年限或学历的人不会被判合乎，也就不会出现在这里。

steps.title: 一个人可能同时过线几个岗位
steps.body: 这个数数的是『按人合并后的卡片』里过线岗位达到两个以上的人。基数约束（having count >= 2）不靠聚合词表硬凑，而是落在物化视图 v_cross_role_candidate 上：视图一行一个人，指标只对它计数。它与各岗位过线人数不可相加——同一个人会被数进多个岗位。

steps.title: 推荐名单有几个名额
steps.body: 名额是岗位内名次落在名单长度内的行数。它与过线人数不是同一个数：过线是资格，名额是名单容量，两者相差多少就是这个岗位的候选人富余度。

steps.title: 名单的分数线
steps.body: 分数线取的是名单内最低的合成分。用它跨岗位比较时要记住：合成分是排序分，不是门槛；比较分数线等于比较不同岗位的评分分布。

steps.title: 最高分与平均分
steps.body: 最高分告诉你天花板，平均分告诉你过线这批人的整体位置。两者都由合成分一列聚合而来，不掺任何缺失填补。

steps.title: 三个没读到
steps.body: 年限、学历、技能三项各有一个未读到标记。未读到既不是零也不是低值：这些人不会通过带相应门槛的岗位判定，所以任何合格率在这里都只能是下界。禁止的写法是把缺失 coalesce 成零——那会把这批人改写成零经验。

steps.title: 没人会的要求技能
steps.body: 每条岗位要求技能都有一个全库会它的人数。这个指标数的是其中为零的条数——零是测量结果，说的是这批候选人里没有人会它，而不是我们没读到技能信息。

steps.title: 按名被拒绝的问题
steps.body: 有些问题这个本体答不了，而它会说出缺哪条声明，而不是给一个看起来对的数。例一：把某个岗位推荐名单前 10 名的**人名与匹配技能列出来**——计算词表只有 aggregate/grain/universe/where/groupBy，没有 orderBy/limit，有序取行不是一个数，缺的是取行词表。例二：某个岗位要什么技能——提交申请的人不少，但职务说明书里没有这一行，定义类无法判真，于是按岗位名拒绝。这两条都不是没想好，是声明边界。

en.title: Walk from a number back to its definition
en.intro: This data is a hiring-season snapshot computed from a pile of résumés and a pile of job descriptions. Every step points at one declared definition; when you press Run, the number is computed by compiled SQL instead of being written in the prose.

steps.title: How many people clear each role
steps.body: Pass counts the candidate rows entailed as members of that role's defined class. It reads no composite score and no rank — the score only decides who to look at first. So this number is a lower bound: people whose years or education were never read are not judged to qualify, and therefore do not appear here.

steps.title: How many people clear more than one role
steps.body: This counts people whose qualified-role count reaches two in the per-person card. The cardinality constraint (having count >= 2) lives in the materialised view v_cross_role_candidate: one row per person, and the metric only counts it. It cannot be added to the per-role counts — the same person is counted under several roles.

steps.title: How many slots a shortlist has
steps.body: Slots are the rows whose in-role rank falls inside the list length. It is not the pass count: passing is eligibility, slots are list capacity, and the gap between them is the candidate surplus for that role.

steps.title: The cut-off score of a shortlist
steps.body: The cut-off is the lowest composite score inside the list. When comparing across roles, remember: the composite score is a ranking score, not a threshold; comparing cut-offs means comparing two roles' score distributions.

steps.title: Highest and average score
steps.body: The maximum tells you the ceiling; the average tells you where the passing group sits. Both aggregate one column, with no gap filling mixed in.

steps.title: Three things we never read
steps.body: Years, education and skills each carry a not-read marker. Not-read is neither zero nor a low value: those people do not pass a role with that threshold, so any pass rate here can only be a lower bound. The forbidden move is to coalesce the gap to zero — that rewrites these people as zero-experience.

steps.title: A required skill nobody has
steps.body: Every required skill has a count of people who hold it. This metric counts the ones whose count is zero — zero is a measurement: nobody in this batch has it, not that we failed to read skills.

steps.title: Questions refused by name
steps.body: Some questions this ontology cannot answer, and it says which declaration is missing instead of returning a plausible number. Example one: list the top ten names and matched skills for a role — the compute vocabulary has aggregate/grain/universe/where/groupBy and no orderBy/limit, so ordered row selection is not a number, and the missing piece is the row-selection vocabulary. Example two: what skills does a role need — the definition class cannot be judged true when the job description lacks that line, so it refuses by name. Neither is an oversight; both are the declared boundary.
